title: December, 2001
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Does Chloe come home. A postcard says she's in Europe. The strip draws Europe from the postcard. Badly. On purpose.

panels.composition: The mailbox. A postcard: a cathedral. Foreign stamp. WOOD reading it in the rain.

image.prompt: a young man reading a postcard of a cathedral with a foreign stamp at a roadside mailbox in the rain, a small dog beside him, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: Her handwriting: 'W — Not coming home. Europe. A city with a river that goes the wrong direction. You'd hate the coffee and drink nine. — C.'

image.prompt: a panel that is the back of a postcard in tiny handwritten capitals with a foreign stamp

panels.composition: Wood at the table drawing the cathedral from the postcard. It comes out looking like the Small Wood grange hall with more windows.
props: pad: a cathedral that looks like a grange hall

image.prompt: a young man at a drawing table drawing a cathedral from a postcard and producing something that looks like a small-town grange hall with extra windows

panels.composition: Christmas Eve, main street. The hardware store's lights. Wood and the dog. Four houses down, her house, dark. He doesn't walk there this year. The strip doesn't either.

image.prompt: a young man and a small dog walking down a rainy main street at night away from a row of houses, hardware store lights behind them, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Europe. He doesn't walk to her house. The strip records the not-walking.
